summary: This is a Snowflake SQL command reference page for CREATE CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER, which creates a new custom classification instance or replaces an existing one in the current or specified schema. It covers the fully qualified name SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER, the syntax with OR REPLACE and IF NOT EXISTS options, identifier rules, and the access requirement of the CLASSIFICATION_ADMIN database role. The page notes that Custom Classification requires Enterprise Edition or higher and that the name is defined and maintained by Snowflake; much of the rest of the scraped text is navigation and boilerplate.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the CREATE CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER command, which creates or replaces a custom classification instance (Enterprise Edition required).
key_facts: The fully qualified name of the object is SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER.
Custom Classification requires Enterprise Edition (or higher) of Snowflake.
The command creates a new custom classification instance or replaces an existing one in the current or specified schema.
The syntax is CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <custom_classifier_name>().
The custom_classifier_name must be unique for the schema in which the object is created.
The parentheses at the end of the identifier are required when creating the object.
The identifier must start with an alphabetic character and cannot contain spaces or special characters unless enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
The command takes no arguments; the page lists Arguments as 'None.'
The account role that creates the object must be granted the CLASSIFICATION_ADMIN database role.
The CLASSIFICATION_ADMIN database role exists in the shared SNOWFLAKE database.
Operating on any object in a schema also requires the USAGE privilege on the parent database and schema.
SNOWFLAKE.DATA_PRIVACY.CUSTOM_CLASSIFIER is a name that Snowflake defines and maintains, so this object name must be used each time an instance is created.
The page's Examples section refers to a representative custom classification example, but no example code is included in the note.
